why: Six parts, six agents, one repository, no coordination between them at build time. The split is written down here so it can be checked mechanically instead of remembered.
readFirst: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md — binding. Every interface in it is a contract between parts.
docs/AGENTS.md — who the fleet is and what an agent holds itself to.
agents/parts/<your part>.json — your own manifest: what you own, what you must never break.
contract: Zero new dependencies. Runtime dep is ethers, devDep is solc, node: builtins are free. Do not add to package.json.

All money, supply, reserve and price arithmetic is BigInt. No float ever touches a balance, a reserve or a price. Floats are permitted only inside weighting math that is immediately quantised back to integers.
Never write a file outside your own "owns" list. Another agent owns the rest and is writing at the same time.
Implement the interfaces in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md exactly. Do not rename, do not widen a signature, do not add a parameter. If the spec is wrong, report it — do not fix it unilaterally.
Every exported function carries a comment saying what it does and why it is shaped that way. Comments explain mechanism and reasoning, not syntax.
Refusals go through core/errors.mjs and carry code, why and fix. Never invent a bare throw with a sentence in it.
Report honestly. A check you could not make pass is an open issue, not a success.

fleet.name: fleet
fleet.title: The build fleet itself — manifests, runner, workflows, and the agent documentation
fleet.summary: Not a part of the software. It owns the files that describe who owns the software, and the scheduled jobs that keep the record alive on machines nobody owns.

checks.name: ownership
checks.why: Two agents editing one file is a lost edit. This runs before the build matrix, not after it.

checks.name: manifests parse
checks.why: A manifest that does not parse cannot be acted on by an agent working alone, which is the only way any of these files get written.

checks.name: claims resolve
checks.why: Every command a check runs must name a file that exists, and every invariant must name a test that is really in the file it points at. This manifest once named twenty-one test files that had never been written; the gate went red for tests that did not exist while the invariants they claimed to hold were held by other files nobody had pointed at.

checks.name: matrix emits
checks.why: .github/workflows/agents.yml fans out over this JSON. If it stops emitting, CI silently runs nothing.

invariants.statement: Every source file in the repository is claimed by exactly one owner. Not zero, not two.

Every check names a command a fresh checkout can run, and every invariant names a test that exists by title in the file it points at. A manifest that names a test that is not there is not a stricter manifest; it is one nobody can act on.
An invariant a part states and nothing holds is declared open with a reason, never deleted and never disguised as a passing check. Every command here prints the open list in full.
invariants.heldBy: node agents/run.mjs --audit — a part's "open" entries must each carry a statement and a reason, and loadFleet refuses the manifest otherwise

invariants.statement: A check whose toolchain is absent is reported SKIP and never PASS, and CI runs the gate with --no-skip after installing, so a skip cannot become permanent by accident.
invariants.heldBy: .github/workflows/agents.yml — the part matrix installs the dependencies and then runs node agents/run.mjs <part> --no-skip

invariants.statement: A part's declared checks are shell commands that a fresh checkout can run. No hidden state, no machine of ours.
invariants.heldBy: .github/workflows/agents.yml — the matrix runs each one on a clean GitHub runner
